newsitem.title: USA: Ohio editor says he stole from charity fund.
newsitem.headline: Ohio editor says he stole from charity fund.

text.p: CINCINNATI - A weekly newspaper editor confessed in his column he stole hundreds of dollars from the newspaper's Christmas fund for the needy and used the money for a gambling addiction involving lottery tickets.
Les Wilson, 71, longtime editor of the Valley Courier in suburban Reading, Ohio, wrote in last week's edition, "I am so ashamed that I hope I am imprisoned and die while there."

Chuck Stidham, Wilson's attorney, told Reuters Tuesday the missing amount was "probably in the neighbourhood of $3,500." No charges have been filed against Wilson, a former sports information director at the University of Louisville, pending further investigation.

Stidham said he hoped the Hamilton County prosecutor's office would let Wilson remain on probation under the condition he make full restitution. "This is a man much beloved in his community -- the kind of guy who would do anything for anyone," he said.

Wilson said in his column that he was forced to sell the 4,600-circulation newspaper in September to maintain his gambling habit but stayed on as editor. He said he had considered suicide but decided that would not solve any of the problems he created.
